game: LAC@BUF Week 3 2026 (kickoff time not in pack; spread/total not saved; weather not saved)

script.base: No market spread or total, so the script is form-only. Buffalo at home has been the more explosive offense through two games (James Cook 34/192, 5.65 YPC; Josh Allen 16/96; Dalton Kincaid 14 targets, 225 yards, 182 air yards) while the Chargers travel with Trey Pipkins (T) and Kayode Awosika (G) out into a Bills blitz (33%) that has crushed Justin Herbert (EPA/db -0.86 vs blitz, +0.09 vs none). Base: Bills stay in front or close late, Cook and Allen carry the closer, Herbert is sped into short throws, and Kincaid stays the pass-game hub unless it becomes a pure run clock. Chargers run defense is the brake (3.14 YPC, only 3 runs of 10+), softened by Dalvin Tomlinson out.
script.flip1: Chargers hang around or lead, so Buffalo abandons the run. Cook's 80.5 rush line dies, Allen's attempts rise, and Kincaid/Khalil Shakir (and DJ Moore or Keon Coleman only if active and full) get a cleaner over path. Herbert still struggles to throw deep if the blitz gets home.
script.flip2: Explosives or a hidden shootout: Elijah Molden (S) is out and LAC allows 10.22 YPA to the left (27 attempts) plus 6 passes of 20+ on 69 attempts, so Allen hits downfield and Quentin Johnston's 103 air yards finally convert. The other flip is a weather slog dragging everything under, but no forecast is saved.

injury_fallout: LAC offense loses Trey Pipkins (T, knee, Out) and Kayode Awosika (G, fibula, Out), so pressure and stuffed runs should rise and quick throws to RBs/TEs should rise while deep WR yards fall; Charlie Kolar (TE, forearm, Out) and Brenen Thompson (WR, quad, Out) are small shares (3 targets each) that funnel to David Njoku (8 targets) and Oronde Gadsden (4), not a new WR1. Trey Lance (Q, groin) is the backup QB and does not change Herbert's role if active. LAC defense loses DT Dalvin Tomlinson (Out), which is the hole in a 3.14 YPC run defense and helps Cook/Allen, plus S Elijah Molden (Out) which helps Buffalo verticals, and CB Rodney Shelley is only Questionable. BUF loses DE T.J. Sanders (Out, illness) and DT Ed Oliver is Questionable (hip), so the 33% blitz may not convert to pressure as often; CB Jordan Hancock is Out, a coverage break for whoever he would have matched, with no charting to name that LAC receiver. G Ar'maj Reed-Adams is Questionable (elbow). DJ Moore (shoulder) and Keon Coleman (ankle) are Questionable, not Out: if limited or inactive their targets move to Kincaid, Shakir (12 targets) and Joshua Palmer (5/77, not in the prop list); if they play full, Kincaid's share is merely the two-week baseline. Sources: pack official injury report and week 1-2 target/carry splits. Final inactives (~90 min pre-kick) are not in the pack.

matchup.shell: No coverage charting, so MOFO/MOFC and man/zone rates are unknown. Location proxy only: BUF allows left 6.24 YPA (29 att), middle 9.41 (22), right 8.52 (25). LAC allows left 10.22 (27), middle 5.64 (14), right 7.0 (25). Middle is Buffalo's bleed and, on a tiny 14-attempt sample, LAC's strength.
matchup.pressure: BUF blitz rate 33%; Herbert EPA/db -0.86 when blitzed vs +0.09 when not. That is the game's clearest scheme fact and it kills deep WR yards while boosting RB/TE checkdowns. LAC blitzes only 25%; Allen EPA/db is +0.36 vs blitz and +0.67 vs none, so he is not pressure-killed. Sanders Out and Oliver Questionable may lower BUF pressure conversion; Pipkins and Awosika Out push LAC protection the other way. Net pressure on Herbert still looks up, but the pass-rush absences are the counter.
matchup.bleeds: BUF bleeds the middle (9.41 YPA) and has allowed 9 passes of 20+ on 83 attempts; the left side is their sound side (6.24). LAC bleeds the left (10.22) and has allowed 6 of 20+ on 69 attempts, with the middle held to 5.64 YPA and the run game held to 3.14 YPC and 3 runs of 10+.
matchup.overlap: Buffalo's primary is Kincaid (14 targets, 182 air yards), which runs into LAC's middle — their best zone, not the left-side bleed — so the core overlap is missing; Molden Out is the only coverage offset for his vertical air yards. LAC's efficient primary is Ladd McConkey (10 targets, 117 yards, 131 air), which would overlap BUF's middle bleed if he is the slot, but 59.5 equals his two-game mean (58.5), so there is no number edge. Johnston (11 targets, 24 yards, 103 air) is not attacking that middle bleed.

No play-by-play, so the 135, the 130, and Johnston's 2.2 yards per target cannot be checked for one-play flukes.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Kincaid beats 57.5 because he is the Bills' passing game through two weeks (14 targets, 225 yards, 182 air yards), both games cleared it by 37+, and Moore/Coleman questionable plus Molden out protect that role even after a partial regression.
edge_players.must_be_true: Kincaid plays a full TE1 snap share, Allen starts, and the game produces a normal pass volume rather than a first-quarter run clock (Cook already at 17 carries a game). A Moore or Coleman limitation helps, it does not hurt.
edge_players.kills_it: BUF leads big and feeds Cook/Allen (34 and 16 carries already) so Kincaid drops under 5 targets, or LAC's middle (5.64 YPA) erases the seam and the 130/95 heater regresses under 57.5. A late inactive is not in the pack.

data_check.notes: Step 8 is incomplete: no projection, no sims, no Pinnacle, no live reprice. Consensus no-vig over is 0.500. A hand read near 0.58 would be +8 pts vs that anchor but is not a 3-sim model and must not be sized; anything at 70%+ would be untrustworthy anyway. Form agrees (130, 95). Matchup data disagrees (LAC middle 5.64 YPA, only 6 explosives on 69 attempts). Per the rule, that disagreement flags this strong read and does not cut it. Dropped leans, not flagged: Cook rush under 80.5 (LAC 3.14 YPC supports it, but mean 96, the 135-yard game, and Tomlinson Out disagree, so the lean dies); Johnston recyds under 36.5 (17 and 7 plus the blitz/EPA split agree, but Hancock Out, Sanders Out, Oliver Questionable, and a regression from 2.2 YPT toward even average efficiency on 5-6 targets clears 36.5, and there is no price); Hampton recyds over 11.5 (checkdown script is real, but he is not in the target table and 0/21 averages 10.5); Knox under 9.5 (usage agrees, price -120 does not beat 0.508 fair). McConkey 59.5 equals his 58.5 mean. No leg from an unpriced market.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and Kincaid over 57.5 lost. LAC sat in a closed middle and took the seam away — that 5.64 YPA on 14 attempts was the real tendency, not noise — Allen leaned on Cook once Buffalo led, and the 130/95 heater was explosive-play noise that regressed to about 4 for 45. Moore and Coleman both played and soaked the targets the questionable tag was supposed to free. A backup safety replaced Molden without a bust. The unmoved 0.500 price was the tell that 57.5 already was the regression landing spot (about 7 targets at ordinary yards per target), and two games were the whole edge.
slip_story: No slip and no bet. This is a single human-flag on a Buffalo pass-volume script (competitive game or Chargers ahead). It loses in a Bills run-clock blowout, so it must not be paired with Cook rush over. It must not be paired with a game under, a Johnston over, or any TD. Correlated friends are not clean: Shakir 40/38 vs 43 has no price, Moore is Questionable, Palmer is not offered. House rule stands: one market, no depth-receiver add, max one flag until inactives and a real sim exist.
